We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

 

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

 

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

 

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

 

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

 

The Role

 

What you’ll do

As our Design Quality & Compliance Engineer, you’ll sit at the heart of Heidi’s mission to make world-class care faster and safer through intelligent, compliant technology. Reporting into the Legal & Regulatory Affairs team, but working day-to-day within Engineering, you’ll be the key link ensuring our agile software development practices remain fully aligned with global medical device and information security standards.

Your core mission is to help ensure that our software design and development activities meet global medical device requirements, leading the practical implementation of IEC 62304 (software lifecycle), ISO 14971 (risk management), and ISO 13485 (quality management systems) within an agile, iterative environment. You’ll help shape how design inputs, verification, validation, and risk controls are captured, reviewed, and evidenced.

This is a hybrid role for someone who can masterfully implement compliance within a modern, agile software culture, enabling engineering teams to build quickly and safely, while ensuring every release stands up to regulatory scrutiny.

 

What you'll do

Drive Medical Device Design Control Processes

  • Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of design control processes across the software lifecycle in alignment with IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and ISO 13485.

  • Partner with engineers and product managers to ensure requirements, risk controls, verification, and validation activities are clearly defined, documented, and traceable.

  • Support the creation and maintenance of technical documentation, including requirements specifications, risk management files, verification reports, and change records.

  • Support external ISO 13485 and Notified Body audits, with a focus on Design and Development aspects.

  • Champion compliance in software development by translating complex and opaque IEC/ISO standards into clear, actionable processes that engineering teams can follow.

     

What we will look for

  • SaMD Experience: Prior experience working on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) or other regulated healthtech products, ideally in a start-up or scale-up environment.

  • Standards: Strong working knowledge of standards such as IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and ISO 27001, and the ability to apply these in practical, developer-friendly ways.

  • Technical Skills: A solid understanding of technical security domains, including cloud security, access control, network security, and secure software development lifecycles.

  • Proactive & Detail-Oriented: A commitment to quality and the ability to drive tasks to completion in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Collaboration & Communication: Excellent communication skills, enabling you to work effectively with internal teams (engineers, product) and manage external partners (auditors, customers).

  • A Bachelor’s degree or higher in a relevant scientific, engineering, regulatory, legal, or governance discipline is a plus.

 

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career.

 

We take care of you.

We offer comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder, a £100/month Healthy Heidi's wellness stipend, a £500 home office budget, a £700 annual learning and development budget, 26 weeks paid primary parental leave and 18 weeks paid secondary parental leave, fertility support up to £7,000, up to four weeks of work from anywhere per year,

Recharge Days after major milestones and busy periods, 10 days per year of clinical leave for eligible clinical roles, and a hybrid working environment with 3 days in the office.

Enterprise Solutions Manager, Managed by Industrious

About Managed by Industrious

For the last decade, companies with real workplace needs have solved them the hard way: building an internal real estate team, running a self-delivery project with a dozen different vendors, and hoping it all comes together on time. Managed by Industrious exists to break that model. We combine the operational expertise we've built running premium flexible workspace at scale with tailored, single-tenant solutions, so landlords and enterprise clients get a fully outsourced, hospitality-driven workplace, without the internal headcount or the fragmented delivery chain. It's our newest product line, and one of the fastest growing parts of the business.

The Opportunity

We're at the point where the model is proven and the demand is real, but the playbook is still being written. This role sits right at the center of that build. You'll take opportunities from a client's first conversation with us through to a signed deal and a live, operating space, working closely with the GM of Enterprise Solutions and a small, senior, fast-moving team. You won't be slotting into a fully formed process. You'll be helping define what that process becomes as the business scales across Europe.


Why Industrious

We've spent the last decade becoming the highest quality provider of flexible workspace in the market. Managed by Industrious is us taking that same operational rigor and hospitality standard and applying it to a completely different kind of client relationship, one where you're building a bespoke, single-tenant solution rather than selling into an existing space. It's early enough that you'll genuinely shape how this product line operates in Europe, and established enough that you're doing it with the backing, brand, and delivery capability of a company that's already proven this model works.

What Might Your Day Look Like

A client reaches out needing a dedicated space for a growing team, say 150 people, in a European city where we don't yet have a foothold for them. You get on the phone to understand what they're actually solving for: who's working there, what the culture needs to feel like, what's non-negotiable and what's flexible. You bring our design team in as a thought partner and land on a brief. From there you're in the market, working with brokerage channels to shortlist two or three sites that could work, and touring the client through them alongside you.

Once you've got a favorite or two, you're building pricing, which means understanding the landlord's lease terms on one side and our own design, build, and operating costs on the other, and pulling all of it into a proposal that's honest about what it will take to deliver. If the client is in, you're moving toward signing high level commercial terms with them and with the landlord at close to the same time, then spending the following weeks getting both to a final agreement.

The moment ink is dry, you're handing a clean, well-briefed project to design and construction, and making sure everything you promised the client is something the business can actually deliver, on time and on budget.

What You Will Own

  • You will manage the full lifecycle of a Managed by Industrious deal, from the first client conversation through to a live, operating space.

  • You will translate what a client says they need into a workable, costed real estate and design solution, working closely with our design team to get there.

  • You will lead landlord and broker relationships on every deal, negotiating lease terms that protect us and set the project up to succeed.

  • You will build the commercial model and client-facing proposal for each opportunity, pulling together lease costs, build costs, and operating costs into a single coherent picture.

  • You will run point on the transaction itself, from high level commercial terms through to final signed agreements with both the client and the landlord.

  • You will hand projects to our design and construction teams with everything they need to deliver on what was promised, and stay close enough through delivery that nothing gets lost in the handoff.

  • You will help build our own playbook as you go, documenting what works so the next deal moves faster than the last one.

  • You will generate your own opportunities when the pipeline calls for it. This isn't a role where you only work what's handed to you.

You Will Love This Role If

  • You get real energy from being the person who makes a complex deal actually happen, not just one piece of it.

  • You're comfortable holding two sides of a negotiation at once, a client who needs to be won over and a landlord who needs to be managed, and you don't lose the thread of either.

  • You'd rather help build a process than inherit a finished one, and you're not precious about the fact that things will change again next month.

  • You want to be trusted with real accountability early, and you're motivated by seeing a project through from a first phone call to a space full of people.

  • You're genuinely energized by the idea that you're building something inside a much larger, established company, without giving up the pace or ownership of a smaller one.

This Role Is Probably Not For You If

  • You want a role with a fixed, well worn process to execute against. This one is still being written, and you'll be one of the people writing it.

  • You'd rather stay on one side of a deal. This role asks you to be genuinely fluent on both the client side and the real estate side, not just conversant in one.

  • Ambiguity slows you down rather than something you push through. Our team is small and things move fast, so you'll often be figuring it out as you go.

  • You're looking for a role where business development isn't part of the job. When the pipeline needs it, you'll be picking up the phone yourself.

What We Are Looking For

  • A track record of managing complex, multi-stakeholder deals or projects through to completion, ideally where you were the person holding the whole thing together rather than one workstream within it.

  • Strong client-facing instincts. You can sit across from a senior stakeholder, understand what they actually need underneath what they're asking for, and turn that into a solution they trust.

  • Comfort working both sides of a transaction. Experience with landlords, brokers, or portfolio-side real estate work is a strong plus, alongside client or account-facing experience.

  • Someone who's excited by the idea of building a new business line inside an established, high quality company, and who wants the accountability that comes with that.

Compensation
We offer a competitive base salary, depending on experience, skills, and role alignment in addition to eligibility for an annual bonus and participation in our long-term incentive program. But compensation is only part of the story.

At Industrious, we believe a good workplace supports the whole person. Not just the work they do. Our benefits are designed to give people the stability, flexibility, and room to grow that make a career sustainable.




Our Benefits May Include:

  • Heavily subsidized medical, dental, and vision plans to support you and your family

We are looking for a Senior Python Developer (or someone operating close to senior level) to join our five-person energy development team. You will help lead the design and implementation of Python packages building on the Home Energy Model that will enable the next generation of energy performance assessment.

You will work closely with DESNZ, external collaborators, our internal domain experts and your dev team, turning tangible and pressing user needs into reliable, maintainable Python software. The team is supportive and high-performing, and the work has a direct impact on carbon reduction.

·       Work across disciplines to integrate tools and deliver results for our customers.

We work collaboratively across the business to provide integrated solutions for a wide range of clients, from national bodies such as DESNZ and the Climate Change Committee (CCC) to forward-thinking local authorities such as Oxfordshire County Council. Our award-winning research, software and product development team builds innovative digital tools, such as our GIS software, Cadence, that sit at the heart of how we deliver our projects.


Essential

·       Strong professional experience as a Python developer, at or near senior level.

·       A track record of building production-grade applications, ideally in data-rich or scientific domains.

·       The ability to write clean, maintainable, well-tested code.

·       Experience line managing or formally mentoring developers, or a clear willingness and motivation to take on line management responsibilities.

·       Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to explain technical ideas clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

·       Experience working in multidisciplinary teams.

Desirable

·       Experience with Pydantic and/or JSON Schema.

·       Familiarity with GitLab CI/CD.

·       A strong grasp of geometry and physics, ideally including building physics.

·       Understanding of decarbonisation and energy systems.

·       Experience supporting the growth of more junior engineers, such as onboarding or coaching.

Aligned to Our Values

·       Excellence: You hold high standards in your code, your solutions and your engineering decisions.

·       Data Driven: You use evidence, analytical thinking and testing to guide your choices.

·       Passion & Urgency: You care about what you build and work with purpose.

About Keyrock

Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 200+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris and New York.

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

 

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Head of Marketing to take full ownership of our marketing strategy, rebrand Keyrock and reposition us as the market evolves from crypto-native to institutional, merging with traditional finance.

This is not a maintenance role. It is a transformation mandate with full discretionary decision-making on how to implement our commercial strategy. You will work as a close strategic partner to the CCO, operating almost as co-marketeers.

The team is lean by design: 2-3 direct reports plus heavy use of AI and agentic tooling. We are looking for someone who inspires and sets direction, not someone who runs campaigns. Operational execution will increasingly be handled by AI agents.

What You Will Do

  • Own and execute the complete rebrand and repositioning of Keyrock in the market

  • Define and drive the marketing strategy across institutional and crypto-native audiences

  • Build a premium, forward-looking brand identity. Think distinctive, audacious, credible to both institutional allocators and crypto-native operators

  • Push information into the market in ways that make people pay attention and take Keyrock seriously

  • Partner closely with the CCO and commercial team to drive measurable commercial impact

  • Build and lead a small, high-impact team augmented by AI tooling

  • Shape how Keyrock is perceived as the industry converges with traditional finance

Who You Are

  • Crypto-native. You have been through market cycles. You understand blockchain technology deeply but you are pragmatic, not ideological. You know this is not a binary world.

  • A brand-builder, not an ops person. You are inspiring, not operational. You set direction, tone and creative vision.

  • An exceptional communicator. You can face institutional allocators who care about regulation and licensing, and crypto-native counterparties who value speed and edge. You switch between both with ease.

  • Confident and assertive. You project authority. You bring conviction and directness - you challenge constructively and don't default to consensus. You bring edge, energy and a slightly audacious style.

  • Human-centric. You connect with people, build followership and bring teams along.

  • Detail-oriented. Despite the strategic focus, you sweat the details on brand consistency, messaging precision and design quality.

  • A challenger mindset. You dare to think differently, question the status quo and push things forward through constructive tension.

Our Recruitment Philosophy

We look for self-aware candidates who bring both the core skills required for the role and a deep alignment with our performance principles. We seek fiercely passionate, mission-driven people who communicate with purpose and practice proactive ownership. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who prioritizes mission over ego, maintains a commercial mindset, and delivers long-term value through pragmatic flexibility.

Experience and Background

Required

  • Significant experience in marketing leadership at a crypto or digital-asset firm

  • Deep understanding of the crypto market, its participants and its culture

  • Track record of building or transforming a brand in a fast-moving, commercially-driven environment

  • Strong communication skills Exceptional fluency in English, both written and spoken.

  • Based in or closely aligned with the CET time zone.

Preferred

  • Experience positioning a firm through a TradFi/crypto convergence narrative

  • Exposure to publicly listed or IPO-track companies

  • Familiarity with EU regulatory environment (MiCA) and how it shapes marketing and financial promotions

  • Experience working with or building AI-augmented marketing functions

Why Keyrock

  • Step-up opportunity. Own the function globally, report directly to the CCO, shape the brand from scratch.

  • Transformation moment. Keyrock is pivoting from appreciated-but-underrated to a firm that commands respect. This is a before-and-after career story.

  • Commercial partnership. Not a siloed marketing role. Deeply embedded in commercial strategy with commission upside.

  • Lean and AI-augmented. Small team, big impact. No bureaucratic bloat. Use agents and tools to move fast.

  • Competitive offer. A competitive compensation package, attractive global benefits, and a performance-based variable.

  • Annual Team Retreats. A yearly offsite dedicated to strategy, celebration of our wins and fun team activities

Product Strategy Analyst - New Customers (UK)

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Product Strategy Analyst

You'll shape how new businesses become iwoca customers – the sign-up flow, the documents we ask for, and the models that decide who gets funded and on what terms.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing.

The team is cross-functional – data scientists, analysts, and software engineers – and sets its own goals and direction. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time.

The role

As the Product Strategy Analyst, you'll run the projects that shape how new businesses join iwoca. You'll steer which experiments the team runs, weighing short-term gains against longer-term bets that compound over time, with customer lifetime value as your key metric.

  • Judgement and strategy. You'll set iwoca's new-customer lending strategy, weighing trade-offs between speed, friction, risk, and decision accuracy. You'll identify drop-off points and commercial opportunities across the conversion funnel, and propose the initiatives that address them.

  • Challenge and experimentation. You'll design, run, and interpret controlled experiments on changes to the customer journey and new loan features. You'll apply statistical thinking so decisions rest on evidence.

  • Autonomy and growth. You'll manage analytical and strategic projects end-to-end, sharing findings and recommendations directly with senior leadership. You'll partner with the Team Lead to shape the team's long-term roadmap, with the expectation of growing into a Team Lead role yourself.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Commercial analytics. You've worked in strategy, analytics, product, finance, or consulting. You understand how to use data to make commercial decisions on revenue, cost, or risk that the business acts on.

  • Quantitative foundations. You have a STEM background (degree or equivalent) in mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, or similar. You reason about uncertainty and calibration, grounded in the underlying statistics.

  • First-principles thinking. You break complex problems into their core parts, decide which to tackle first, and iterate systematically to a solution.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • AI leverage. You've built AI workflows, or used AI to produce analysis or prototypes beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

Bonus:

  • Experimentation. You have designed, run, and interpreted controlled experiments, including A/B tests, to inform product or policy decisions.

  • Cross-functional delivery. You have worked closely with engineering or data science teams to get analytical insight into production systems.

  • Customer journey analytics. You have analysed and improved a customer journey, balancing conversion, risk, and long-term value.

  • Coding abilities. You can code for analysis, automation, or prototypes - whether directly or via AI coding tools like Claude Code.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 to £80,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

About The Role

The Implementation Team is responsible for the onboarding of all our Premium and Pro customers on the Perk platform, and providing recommendations to optimize the customer experience. We guide new customers from signup to launch, providing consultative, administrative, technical, and educational support to maximize the customer’s experience with the Perk platform.

As an Implementation Specialist, you must be a change management and consultative expert who digs in deeply to understand customer needs and provides customers with a tailored solution that meets their needs. You'll use your platform expertise and stakeholder management skills to build a bridge between platform capabilities and customer expectations. In order to serve the customer beyond the bounds of the platform you'll produce a thoughtful rollout plan that accurately covers the scope of the specific customer’s needs, including immediate travel and a long term success. As an IS, you'll be both a mentor and an example to the Implementation team and across the Revenue organization.
The IS ensures that new customers are fully prepared to use Perk to book their business travel, by executing platform configuration, providing technical support and troubleshooting, and user readiness. This includes configuring customer accounts to their specifications and requirements, providing proactive support on any integrations, as well as coordinating and executing tailored training sessions with key customer stakeholders.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Provide the first impression of Perk to all customers in your portfolio and serve as the first point of contact for customers during the implementation process.

  • Define the best onboarding strategy, leading the change within the customer´s org and providing support in any technical aspects related to the integrations and account setup. That means preparing and executing onboarding plans through the use of project management.

  • Carry out consultative conversations with customers to collect their requirements.

  • Proactively providing customers with recommendations with your experience and data-driven best practice recommendations.

  • Drive customer onboarding forward by providing influential recommendations and creating urgency for customer stakeholders.

  • Manage the rollout of a new platform for your customers; providing guides, templates, and recommendations to the customer for how to ensure adoption and long-term success of the platform.

  • Take full ownership of timeline, rollout plan and handling of the account while the account is in implementation, including directing work through the internal team supporting customers and, in essence, being the subject matter expert in the area of change management.

  • Coordinate and conduct training sessions for newly onboarded customers, including executive-level stakeholders and company-wide training.

  • Validate customer configuration and account satisfaction by monitoring customer booking behaviour post-implementation and proactively offering support or recommendations.

  • Embrace a pattern of execution, assess, improve, repeat and evolve as the team and organization evolve.

  • Take on additional projects related to IS Team alignment with other departments. Ensure that project team members have a clear understanding of timelines, tasks, risks and issues.

 

What We’re Looking For

  • Demonstrated relevant professional experience, either as an Implementation Specialist, Sales, Customer Care, Account Management, Project Management or other related roles.

  • Demonstrated overachievement against targets/goals & expectations in previous roles.

  • English fluency is essential; strong comprehension, writing, and verbal communication skills are required.

Additional attributes of an Implementation Specialist

  • Proven track record of successfully managing and delivering complex projects.

  • Although Implementation Specialists need to be tech-savvy and understand some basic technical concepts in the area of integrations and open APIs, they do not need to be experts in this area right away.

  • Solid level of Project Management, Persuasive Communication, Technical/Business Acumen and Customer Centric Quality Control skills.

  • A customer-first mentality; you’ll focus on ensuring a smooth onboarding for your customers and must understand what they need to be a happy customer for the long term.

  • Willingness to seek out ways to improve and develop a mindset of continuous improvement.

  • Excited by challenges and have a personal drive to make a difference.

  • Excellent problem-solving and process optimization skills, with the ability to identify inefficiencies and implement effective solutions.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and managing competing priorities.

What We Offer

  • Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

  • Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

  • Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

  • Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

  • Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

  • Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

  • Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

  • Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

  • Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

  • Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

  • Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

  • Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

  • Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

The Process

1) A 20-minute screening call with our Talent Acquisition Partner

2) A 1-hour practical assessment presentation with our Hiring Manager

3) A 30-minute interview with our IS Country Manager

4) A 30-minute in-person culture‑fit interview in our Birmingham hub

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

The team

At blp, dedicated engineering teams own individual products such as invoices, customer orders, and order confirmations. The Platform Team owns what all of them are built on: shared services and APIs, the data access layer, and the component and design system that shape how the product looks and behaves.

The team's focus has been the frontend platform, and we are now deliberately extending that ownership deeper into the stack. You would be central to that shift, with real influence over how the platform layer gets defined rather than inheriting someone else's blueprint.

 

About the role

We are looking for a fullstack engineer with a strong backend center of gravity who enjoys designing reliable systems, thinking rigorously about correctness, and applying strong software fundamentals to real-world operational problems.

Platform touches both client facing features as well as internal tooling. The capabilities we own are the ones our users touch most often: how workflows and dashboards are configured, how fast a screen full of exceptions loads, how consistently permissions behave, how reliably a release reaches production. When the platform is right, every product team ships better software faster, and that lands directly with the tens of thousands of people who use blp every day. Platform decisions here are judged by what they do for our users, not by internal elegance.

 

What you'll do

  • Build the Foundation: Design and develop the shared backend services and APIs that our product teams depend on, with clear contracts and abstractions that fit how they actually work.

  • Drive User Impact: Work with product teams and business stakeholders to understand where the platform is holding them back, communicate trade-offs openly, and turn that into concrete improvements our users feel.

  • Own Reliability and Correctness: Build and operate systems with a strong focus on robustness, and improve them continuously through careful analysis and iteration. Managing entropy in a complex system is part of the job, and we expect you to adapt accordingly.

  • Build Great Software: Write clean, maintainable, high-quality code across the stack. Conduct code reviews and contribute to a culture of technical excellence.

  • Shape Architecture: Collaborate on system design, tech stack decisions, and platform boundaries, optimizing for scalability, performance, and maintainability.

  • Lead and Influence: Guide technical direction on major initiatives such as migrations and platform capabilities, and mentor team members along the way.

  • Promote Innovation and Collaboration: Work closely with colleagues to continuously improve processes, tools, and team practices, fostering a culture of learning and growth.

The tech stack includes Golang, React/TypeScript, Python, various ML models, MySQL, F#, Docker images deployed on a Kubernetes cluster in our cloud infrastructure (GCS, AWS, or Azure), and GitHub CI/CD.

 

What you'll bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a closely related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years of experience in a software engineering role, with a clear backend focus.

  • Genuine fullstack capability: comfortable working in a modern React/TypeScript codebase, even if backend is where you do your deepest work.

  • Experience with functional programming concepts or languages.

  • Passionate about software craftsmanship: strong understanding of core engineering principles including type systems, composition, testing, Clean Code, and Clean Architecture.

  • Product thinking: ability to translate business problems into precise requirements, specifications, and ultimately into code.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset: link your daily work to team and company goals, balance cost and benefit, deliver high-quality solutions efficiently.

  • Ownership: take responsibility for your technical work, for the platform we build, and for the team we shape.

  • Abstraction and efficient communication: simplify complex systems, identify core concepts, and communicate complex ideas clearly.

 

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with distributed systems, Kubernetes, or cloud infrastructure.

  • Experience with ERP systems, finance, procurement, or supply chain processes.

  • Background in a platform, infrastructure, or developer experience team.

  • Experience with large-scale migrations or incremental modernization of an existing codebase.

  • German language skills.

 

What we value

We value engineers who think deeply about systems, care about correctness, and take pride in building a platform that is understandable, maintainable, and reliable. Because our work sits underneath every product team, we also value people who can hold both perspectives at once: the rigor to get the foundation right, and the product sense to know which foundation is worth building.

 

What you'll get

  • Ownership of the platform layer. Every product team builds on it, and you have real influence over how it's defined.

  • Work that reaches real scale. It lands directly with the tens of thousands of people who use blp every day, not just internal elegance.

  • A high-caliber engineering culture. Collaborative, and one that values correctness and craftsmanship.

  • Structured onboarding. Continuous learning follows as the platform's scope grows.

This role is available on-site in Zurich, London, Barcelona or remotely within Europe.

About Us 

Avenir Collective. Building the future of beauty, personal care and lifestyle brands. 

We acquire and scale high-potential consumer brands, bringing together the capital, people and operating expertise to turn strong brands into enduring businesses. Our difference is that we are operators, actively managing our brands and providing the capabilities, infrastructure and expertise they need to scale, while preserving the product, purpose and consumer connection that make each brand special. 

We’re building a connected house of brands where great people, brands and ideas come together. If you’re excited by building businesses, solving problems and working with a collaborative, entrepreneurial team, we’d love to hear from you. 

Your role at a Glance 

The commercially minded, entrepreneurial Head of Product leads the end-to-end product strategy, innovation and lifecycle management across Avenir Collective's portfolio of beauty, personal care and lifestyle brands. This is a high-impact, group-level leadership role responsible for defining and scaling our product capability, ensuring we continue to deliver differentiated, consumer-led products that drive brand growth, commercial performance and long-term competitive advantage.

Reporting to the Chief Brand Officer, this role acts as the strategic product leader for the organisation, partnering closely with Brand Managers, who define brand strategy and positioning, to translate consumer insight, market opportunity and commercial objectives into market-leading product portfolios. You own the innovation roadmap, end-to-end product lifecycle, commercial evaluation, regulatory excellence and supplier partnerships, whilst building the systems, governance and processes required to support a scalable, multi-brand business.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the future of Avenir Collective's beauty and personal care portfolio, while supporting expansion across adjacent lifestyle categories and integrating future acquisitions into a unified product capability. Working cross-functionally with Brand, Commercial, Supply Chain and Finance, you will ensure product innovation remains a strategic driver of growth, balancing consumer desirability, operational excellence, commercial viability and regulatory compliance

Location & Flexibility

  • Full-time, permanent role based at our modern office in Holborn, London

  • 40 hours per week, 9 am to 6 pm with a one-hour lunch

  • This position is hybrid, with the expectation to go to the office 3 days per week

Product Strategy & Portfolio

  • Own the product strategy and innovation roadmap across our portfolio of beauty, personal care and lifestyle brands, aligned to brand, consumer and commercial priorities. 

  • Identify and assess new product, category and portfolio opportunities using consumer insight, market trends, competitive intelligence and commercial analysis. 

  • Lead portfolio prioritisation and investment decisions, developing robust business cases and ensuring resources are focused on the highest-value opportunities.

  • Own the end-to-end product lifecycle from ideation and development through launch, optimisation and retirement. 

  • Drive innovation across formulations, ingredients, formats, packaging and product experience, with a particular focus on beauty and personal care.

  • Partner with Brand, Commercial, Operations, Supply Chain and Finance to ensure products are differentiated, commercially viable, scalable and successfully launched. 

Quality, Regulatory & Commercial Governance

  • Own product quality, regulatory compliance, testing, claims substantiation, labelling and documentation across all products and markets. 

  • Develop strategic supplier and manufacturing partnerships that support innovation, quality, speed to market and commercial value. 

  • Own product costing, margin and development investment governance, ensuring product decisions deliver sustainable commercial returns. 

  • Oversee product IP and integrity, including product naming, trademarks and protection of proprietary innovation. 

Leadership

  • Establish scalable processes and ways of working that support portfolio growth and the successful integration of future acquired brands.

About Level Zero
Level Zero is pioneering next-generation biosensor technology for precise, real-time monitoring of critical endocrine biomarkers. Recognised as one of the top 20 startups across all categories worldwide at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024 - and backed by top-tier organisations like SOSV and Entrepreneur First - we’re pushing the boundaries of biochemistry and nanotechnology to revolutionize personalised health.

Founded by two seasoned engineers, we bring extensive experience in R&D, technical innovation, and commercial strategy to transform the way people monitor their health. Our mission is bold: to revolutionise health management by delivering clinical-grade data directly to individuals, wherever they are.

We’re seeking driven innovators to join us in pushing the boundaries of biosensing and health tech, making personalised health monitoring a reality for everyone. To achieve this ambitious vision, we’re assembling the best team in the world - dedicated to turning cutting-edge science into life-changing, real-world solutions.
 

About the Role

We are seeking a lead biosensor scientist to drive the development and commercialisation of our continuous aptamer sensor platform. The ideal candidate will have proven expertise in developing continuous monitoring devices for regulated healthcare applications, demonstrated experience transitioning research-stage sensors into manufacturing-ready products, and a track record working with in vivo validation studies and large-scale analytical verification programs.

This is a full-time, in-person role primarily based in London.


What you'll do
  • Lead the development and optimisation of electrochemical continuous sensor systems from bench concept through manufacturing readiness.
  • Design and execute large-scale analytical verification studies, including multi-parameter performance characterisation, stability assessments, and biocompatibility validation.
  • Oversee in vivo validation studies in human subjects and troubleshoot sensor performance in clinical settings.
  • Define manufacturing processes, material specifications, and quality control parameters aligned with regulatory expectations and QMS frameworks.
  • Engage directly with regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) to define performance specifications and shape submission strategy.
  • Lead cross-functional efforts with electrochemistry, microfabrication, and manufacturing to translate designs into scalable production.
  • Develop technical documentation packages (CMC, analytical performance dossiers) for regulatory submissions and investor communications.
  • Mentor junior scientists and technicians in sensor characterisation and assay validation methodologies.

    • What You Bring
  • A Ph.D. degree in electrochemistry, materials science, biomedical engineering, or related discipline, with specific focus on electrochemical biosensors. Minimum 4 years of industry experience commercialising continuous monitoring or diagnostic sensor technologies.

    • The ideal candidate will possess expertise in the following areas:

  • Deep experience in electrochemical sensor development-particularly amperometric, potentiometric, or impedance-based platforms-with demonstrated progression from research concept to clinical or commercial application.
  • Proven track record managing regulatory submissions (FDA 510(k), De Novo, or CE marking) for continuous monitoring devices.
  • Strong experience designing and executing large-scale analytical verification studies including stability, accuracy, precision, and matrix interference assessments.
  • Demonstrated experience working with in vivo validation studies, including study design, data interpretation, and regulatory reporting.
  • Knowledge of manufacturing readiness, scale-up strategy, and GMP-compatible processes.
  • Proven ability to operate in QMS-ready environments with familiarity of ISO 13485, design controls, and regulatory compliance frameworks.
  • Understanding of biocompatibility, sterility, and shelf-life requirements for implantable or skin-worn continuous devices.
  • Proficiency in surface chemistry, material selection, and biointerface optimisation.
  • Expertise in aptamer-based biorecognition elements and aptamer optimisation for continuous monitoring applications.

    • Nice to have:

  • Experience with microneedle or transdermal ISF technologies.
  • Familiarity with SELEX or aptamer discovery workflows.
  • Experience with MEMS & electrode microfabrication processes.

    • Who You Are
    We value culture as much as we value technical expertise, creating an environment that’s equal parts collaboration, curiosity, and fun.

    We’re a fast-paced, mission-driven young team on a quest to make a lasting impact, fueled by uncompromising integrity, unwavering support for one another, and the thrill of exploring uncharted territories. Our passion for excellence drives everything we do, and we welcome individuals who share our commitment to shaping the future.

    If our vision excites you, here are the qualities we look for:
    • You live and breathe integrity, tackling challenges with honesty and transparency
    • You’re a self-starter who loves diving into the unknown, collaborating on complex problems, and taking full ownership of results
    • You excel at open, clear communication and see every piece of feedback as a springboard for growth—especially in a science and data-focused environment
    • You’re motivated by creating real impact, particularly when it comes to advancing human health
    • You strike a balance between independence and collaboration, knowing when to seek support or invite others to join in
    • You’re confident in defending your ideas, while also valuing respectful, constructive debate as a path to better solutions
    • You thrive in the dynamic atmosphere of a startup, constantly evolving your skill set and fearlessly applying what you learn

    What We Offer
    • A full-time role with a competitive salary and equity options, reflecting our value in your expertise and potential
    • An environment where you’ll collaborate directly with the founding team at a leading biosensor startup, gaining access to industry experts and thought leaders
    • The chance to grow with us, including ample opportunities for leadership, career advancement, and exploration
    • Travel to New York and other potential sites for R&D purposes
    • The excitement of working on cutting-edge technology, shaping strategic decisions, and driving innovation at an early-stage venture alongside a superstar team

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

The role

Checkout.com is looking for an enthusiastic Engineer I to join Finance Technology with a focus on Workday Adaptive Planning. Adaptive Planning supports finance, workforce, sales, and operational planning, giving teams a shared platform for budgeting, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and decision-making.

This is an early-career engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in finance systems, application configuration, data integration, and operational support. You will work with Finance, Finance Technology, Data, and wider Corporate Technology teams to keep planning processes reliable, well-controlled, and easy to operate.

You will have support from more senior engineers for complex design decisions, but you will be expected to work independently for longer periods on well-defined configuration, integration, support, and continuous-improvement tasks. This reflects Checkout’s Engineer 1 expectations: delivering small-to-medium-sized work, supporting common operational flows, communicating clearly, and taking ownership of the quality of what you deliver.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Configure, maintain, and enhance Adaptive Planning models, dimensions, versions, levels, accounts, sheets, reports, dashboards, and planning workflows under appropriate guidance.

  • Support the delivery of budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, scenario modelling, and management reporting capabilities for Finance and business stakeholders.

  • Build and support data loads and integrations between Adaptive Planning, Workday Financials, Workday HCM, and other approved internal or third-party systems.

  • Maintain data mappings, transformation rules, validation checks, and reconciliation processes so that planning data is complete, accurate, and traceable.

  • Monitor scheduled loads and integration tasks, investigate failures, and resolve common data or configuration issues within agreed service levels.

  • Triage incidents and service requests, identifying root causes and escalating complex or high-risk issues with clear evidence and recommended next steps.

  • Partner with Finance stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into maintainable system configuration, reporting, or integration changes.

  • Contribute to the assessment and delivery of future analytics data flows, including the potential use of Adaptive Planning data in BigQuery and management analytics.

  • Participate in testing, regression testing, release preparation, and controlled deployment of Adaptive Planning changes.

  • Follow change-control, access-management, data-quality, and audit requirements relevant to financial systems and planning data.

  • Create clear documentation, support guides, data dictionaries, integration runbooks, and knowledge-base articles so that operational knowledge is shared rather than held by one person.

  • Identify recurring manual work or failure patterns and propose practical automation and process improvements.

What we’re looking for

Essential experience and skills

  • Experience in a finance systems, enterprise applications, data, reporting, or integration environment.

  • Practical experience with Workday Adaptive Planning, or strong experience with a comparable planning, performance-management, ERP, or finance application and a clear ability to learn Adaptive quickly.

  • Understanding of core finance planning concepts such as budgets, forecasts, actuals, variance analysis, allocations, dimensions, hierarchies, and scenarios.

  • Experience configuring or supporting structured data models, application workflows, reports, dashboards, or business rules.

  • Ability to work with data imports, exports, mappings, transformations, validations, and reconciliations.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to break down an issue, gather evidence, identify likely causes, and communicate findings clearly.

  • Good attention to detail and an understanding of why accuracy, access control, auditability, and repeatability matter in finance systems.

  • Ability to manage small-to-medium-sized tasks independently while knowing when to ask for help or escalate.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Finance and Technology stakeholders.

Desirable experience

  • Workday Adaptive Planning certification or implementation experience.

  • Experience with Adaptive Planning Integration, Planning Data Loader, APIs, or equivalent enterprise planning integration tooling.

  • Experience integrating planning systems with Workday Financials, Workday HCM, an ERP, a data warehouse, or a reporting platform.

  • Familiarity with SOX controls, financial audit requirements, data privacy, and segregation of duties.

  • Experience supporting month-end, budget, forecast, or management-reporting cycles.

  • Exposure to Agile delivery, ticket-driven change management, incident management, or service-management practices.

What success looks like

After the first 6–12 months, you will be able to:

  • Support common Adaptive Planning configuration, data-load, and reporting requests with limited supervision.

  • Diagnose and resolve routine integration or data-quality issues using a structured troubleshooting approach.

  • Deliver small-to-medium-sized enhancements from requirement clarification through testing, documentation, and controlled release.

  • Explain key planning data flows, mappings, dependencies, and operational controls to Finance and Technology colleagues.

  • Improve the reliability or efficiency of at least one recurring planning or finance-technology process.

  • Maintain accurate, useful documentation and contribute positively to team ceremonies, reviews, and knowledge-sharing sessions.

Working style and behaviours

We are looking for someone who:

  • Takes ownership of tasks and follows through on commitments.

  • Acts with urgency and accountability when issues affect Finance or business reporting.

  • Is curious about how finance processes, data, and technology fit together.

  • Communicates clearly, especially when explaining risk, blockers, trade-offs, or support impact.

  • Welcomes feedback and actively develops their technical and domain knowledge.

  • Collaborates generously and shares knowledge so the team does not depend on a single subject-matter expert.

  • Looks for durable automation and simpler operating processes rather than repeatedly working around the same manual problem.

Why join Finance Technology?

You will work on systems that sit at the centre of how Checkout.com plans, forecasts, reports, and makes financial decisions. The role offers the opportunity to develop a broad foundation across enterprise applications, finance processes, integrations, data quality, controls, and automation while working closely with experienced Finance and Technology professionals.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

Venez rejoindre l'IMT Mines Alès, grande école de prestige qui se classe parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs sur le plan national et mondial et implantée à Alès, ville à taille humaine, capitale des Cévennes où la qualité de vie est fortement appréciée par ses habitants.

Créée en 1843, IMT Mines Alès compte à ce jour 1400 élèves (dont 250 étrangers) et 380 personnels. L’école dispose de 3 centres de recherche et d’enseignement de haut niveau scientifique et technologique, qui œuvrent dans les domaines des matériaux et du génie civil (C2MA), de l’environnement et des risques (CREER), de l’intelligence artificielle et du génie industriel et numérique (CERIS). Elle dispose de 12 plateformes technologiques et compte 1600 entreprises partenaires. Pour en savoir plus : https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr

Vous êtes rattaché(e) au Centre de Recherche et d’Enseignement en Environnement et Risques (CREER) de l'IMT Mines Alès et dans l'unité de recherche : HSM.

Ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet PREV’IA qui s’intéresse à la connaissance et à la prévision des ressources en eaux de la nappe plioquaternaire de la plaine de Roussillon, et de la source du Lez qui alimente Montpellier en eau potable.

Votre travail s’inscrira dans la continuité d’une thèse en cours au sein de l’UMR HSM (équipe HYTAKE), portant sur la durabilité de la ressource en eau karstique (aquifère du Lez) alimentant une métropole méditerranéenne (Montpellier) en contexte de changement climatique.

 

Votre mission :

  • Utiliser les concepts émergeants dans les approches de « Physics Informed Machine Learning » (PIML) pour évaluer les intérêts d’une synergie en modélisation hydrogéologique : (1) à base conceptuelle d’une part et (2) à base de réseaux de neurones informés, ou complémentés, par la physique. L’approche PIML (Physics Informed Machine Learning) est développée, avec deux courants : (i) les Physics Informed Architecture (PIA) : intégration de connaissances physiques dans l’architecture du modèle (couches cachées) ; et (ii) les Physics Informed Loss Function (PILF) : combinaison de modélisations physiques (équations différentielles) et boîte noire, fusionnées dans la fonction de coût (terme de régularisation). Les deux méthodes pourront être explorées. Les modèles proposés pourront être utilisés pour déterminer l’évolution de certaines grandeurs hydrologiques en réponse au changement climatique.

Vous trouvez plus d’information sur le descriptif du poste ci-dessous :

https://partage.imt.fr/index.php/s/ANqeAPRfSdBfnof

Compétences, connaissances et expériences requises :

  • Expérience en machine Learning pour la modélisation des phénomènes naturels complexes

IMT Atlantique, reconnue internationalement pour la qualité de sa recherche, est une école d’ingénieurs de premier plan sous la tutelle du ministère de l'industrie et du numérique, classée dans les trois principaux classements internationaux (THE, SHANGHAI, QS).

 

Le poste est ouvert sur le campus de Rennes au sein du département SRCD (Systèmes Réseaux, Cybersécurité et Droit du numérique). Le département SRCD est composé de 24 enseignant.e.s-chercheurs.euses permanent.e.s, plus de 10 post-doctorant.e.s et ingénieur.e.s contractuel.le.s, et 30 doctorant.e.s. Ses domaines d'activité recouvrent tous les aspects de l'enseignement et de la recherche en systèmes et réseaux au sens large, en cybersécurité, et en droit et économie des activités numériques. Dans le cadre de ses activités de recherche, la personne recrutée rejoindra l’équipe SOTERN (Self Protecting the Future Internet) du département D2 du laboratoire IRISA (UMR CNRS 6074), l'un des plus grands laboratoires de recherche français (+ de 850 personnes) dans le domaine de l'informatique et des nouvelles technologies de l'information.

Enjeux et profil attendu sur le thématique de recherche

 

Deux enjeux majeurs présentent actuellement un impact conséquent sur la recherche et l’innovation en Cybersécurité. D’un côté, l’intelligence artificielle par ses développements récents et les attendus pour les années à venir décuple les possibilités offertes aux attaquants pour mettre en œuvre de nouvelles attaques, tout autant qu’aux structures défensives (type SOC par exemple) pour détecter, corréler et contrer des incidents de sécurité. D’un autre côté, les cibles des attaques évoluent et les architectures déployées dans les réseaux opérationnels (systèmes industriels, réseaux intra-véhiculaires, avionique, opérateurs d’importance vitale) nécessitent de nouveaux moyens de détection et protection face à une menace grandissante.

Le profil recherché pour ce poste s’inscrit ainsi dans la thématique de la sécurité des réseaux au sens large. Il sera plus spécifiquement recherché soit une expertise relative aux architectures, protocoles et algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle pour la sécurité des réseaux ou de l’IA (apprentissage fédéré, sécurité des architectures d’IA type Model Context Protocol (MCP), etc.), soit une expertise sur la sécurité des réseaux opérationnels (OT) quel qu’en soit le cadre applicatif.  

 

Enjeux et profil attendu en enseignement

 

Positionnée sur 3 campus attractifs, IMT Atlantique affiche une forte dynamique internationale tout en restant à taille humaine. Dans ces différents cursus BAC+5 (formations d’ingénieurs et de masters-DNM), les étudiants sont confrontés, via des approches pédagogiques variées, à des situations-problèmes concrets. L’école a ainsi pour ambition de former de jeunes professionnels à fort potentiel, capables de mobiliser un large spectre de compétences en situation réelle, dans des environnements (production, recherche, création d’activité, etc.) et des domaines socio-économiques variés.

 

Impliqué tant en tronc commun que dans les parcours électifs, la personne recrutée contribuera aussi bien dans sa spécialité Cybersécurité que dans des activités transverses, interdisciplinaires ou en lien avec des entreprises : tutorat de projets / stages, soutenances, accompagnement, etc. La personne recrutée sera encouragée à contribuer, dans un esprit de collaboration, à l’évolution cohérente des programmes d’études, en proposant de nouveaux projets, programmes et méthodologies pédagogiques, particulièrement inspirés et soutenus par les exigences et les partenariats industriels. https://www.imt-atlantique.fr/fr/formation

 

En cohérence avec le profil de la personne candidate, il sera demandé de prendre en main les thématiques d’enseignement parmi les suivantes : IA et Cybersécurité (IA offensive, IA pour la protection des infrastructures, sécurité de l’IA), Sécurité des systèmes industriels, participation puis prise de responsabilité de l’organisation du CTF Hack’lantique, et plus largement une participation aux différents enseignements en Cybersécurité.

 

Responsabilité collective et implication dans le développement économique

En effet une attention particulière sera portée sur la capacité du candidat à s’impliquer dans la vie collective de l’école : contribuer, ou piloter des projets transverses (par exemple sur la transition écologique, prendre des responsabilités (programmes de formation, projets de recherche, équipes pédagogiques ou de recherche) ou participer à des instances : comité de l’enseignement, conseil d’école, comité social d’administration.

En outre dans un environnement de relations privilégiées avec de grands partenaires industriels nationaux et internationaux, ainsi qu’un réseau dense de PME, Start up, l’enseignant chercheur recruté contribuera au rayonnement de l’école et au développement économique, notamment au travers de la valorisation de ses travaux par le dépôt de brevet ou le transfert de technologies. Avec 257 enseignants-chercheurs permanents, 2450 étudiants dont 399 doctorants, IMT Atlantique produit chaque année 655 publications et lève 28.3M€ de fonds de recherche.
